sentences.text: The detection workflow begins when the North Lookout Camera Mast, South Lookout Camera Mast, or Horizon Ridge Drone Dock provides an observation that may indicate a new ignition.
Each observation is time stamped, georeferenced, and associated with equipment status before it is evaluated as operational evidence.
The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine receives the observation context and normalizes image, thermal, and weather attributes into a common event record.
Smoke indications are initially assessed for plume texture, persistence, motion, and contrast against the background terrain.
Thermal cues are treated as supporting evidence unless they persist across sequential frames or align with a visible smoke indication.
The Smoke Classifier Module produces the Ridge Shadow Mask when terrain-shadow conditions could otherwise inflate a smoke confidence score.
The analytics score is not considered a declaration of fire, because atmospheric glare, dust, vehicle exhaust, and cloud shadow can produce similar signatures.
MesoWest Weather Fusion Node provides local wind, humidity, temperature, and stability context that helps determine whether an indication is plausible for active combustion.
When the automated confidence level exceeds the screening threshold, the Caldera Incident Command Portal opens a triage case for human review.
The Duty Detection Officer reviews the triage case, compares current imagery with recent frames, and checks whether the indication is growing, drifting, or disappearing.
The Duty Detection Officer may request a fresh pan, tilt, or zoom view from the nearest fixed camera when the initial frame is ambiguous.
If terrain, smoke column height, or occlusion prevents a clear fixed-camera view, the Drone Tasking Service may prepare a verification task for the Horizon Ridge Drone Dock.
The Drone Pilot Operator confirms that the proposed verification task is safe for launch conditions and consistent with current operating constraints.
The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater supports voice coordination when field observers or aviation personnel can provide independent confirmation from their location.
The Air Attack Supervisor may be referred to by the alias Redtail during radio coordination, but the operational record uses Air Attack Supervisor.
The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console may be referred to by the alias Marigold during dispatch coordination, but the operational record uses Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console.

Confirmation requires at least one persistent smoke indication or thermal cue, plus either independent sensor corroboration, field report corroboration, or a direct human visual judgment recorded by an authorized reviewer.
A suspected ignition remains in triage when evidence is inconsistent, stale, or limited to a single low-confidence source.
The Caldera Incident Command Portal records the reason for each triage decision so later operators can understand whether the case was advanced, held, or dismissed.
When the confirmation rule is satisfied, the incident record is advanced to the Confirmed Ignition State and becomes available for suppression planning.
The Confirmed Ignition State includes the best known location, confidence basis, observation history, reviewer identity, and current recommended coordination posture.
Crewline Mobile Tablet users receive only the confirmed incident context that has been released for field distribution by the command workflow.
East Retardant Loading Pump sends the Retardant Batch Slip after a load cycle is metered and sealed.
If air operations are constrained, the Caldera Incident Command Portal can associate the incident with the Airspace Restricted State before aircraft tasking is attempted.
Dismissed cases remain searchable for audit and model improvement, but they do not create a suppression assignment or public incident notification.
